context_spans.label: the section prose: the ultrafilter construction of the rings Z-A, the fibre product formula Z of A cap B equals the fibre product of Z-A and Z-B over Z of A union B, the joint surjectivity with no finite subfamily, and the full proof of Claim I by the torsion-free, torsion and general cases

standard_prerequisites: A nonprincipal ultrafilter U on the set P of prime numbers: every subset of P or its complement lies in U, U is closed under finite intersection, and no finite set lies in U
For A in U the ring Z-A is the localization of the integers at the multiplicative set generated by the primes in A; its spectrum is the generic point plus the closed primes outside A
Localization is exact and commutes with tensor products; a torsion abelian group decomposes as the direct sum of its p-primary components

The equalizer condition for a family of flat ring maps A to A-i on modules: M equals the equalizer of the two natural maps from the product of M tensor A-i to the product over pairs of M tensor A-i tensor A A-j
core_obligations: The family of flat maps Z to Z-A indexed by the nonprincipal ultrafilter U is jointly surjective on spectra but no finite subfamily is, since any finite subfamily factors through the localization away from a single prime

For the equalizer property, first take M torsion free: each Z-A embeds into the rationalization M-P, and the equalizer statement reduces to M equal to the intersection of the localizations M-A inside M tensor Q; this holds because for every prime p the complement of the singleton p lies in U, so already the intersection of the localizations at the primes two and three recovers M

Next take M torsion: M decomposes as the direct sum of its p-primary parts, and M-A is the direct sum over primes outside A; an element of the product lying in the equalizer has components x-p indexed by the complements of singletons, and the equalizer identities force all but finitely many of these to vanish; if infinitely many were nonzero, partition the support into two infinite parts T and T-prime, one of which, say T, is not in the ultrafilter, so T is the complement of some A in U, contradicting the finiteness just established

In general, chase the short exact sequence of M through its torsion subgroup and quotient in the large nine-term diagram; exactness of localization together with the two settled cases proves the equalizer property for M

No finite subfamily of the maps Z to Z-A satisfies the equalizer property, since the finite subfamily factors through a localization away from one prime and modules supported at that prime fail the equalizer condition
proof_roadmap: Build the ultrafilter family and record joint surjectivity without finite subfamilies
Prove the equalizer property in the torsion-free and torsion cases
Chase the torsion exact sequence for a general module and exclude finite subfamilies
